exposure: Infrastructure changes (office redesign, expanded point-of-care services, hospital privileges for family physicians)
Independence from hospital and university control
cohort: The study included 13,926 consecutive family medicine deliveries over eighteen years, representing patients receiving obstetric care from family physicians in a chronically underserved urban area.
finding: This model of independent family medicine practice, with infrastructure changes and expanded point-of-care services, provides a framework for retaining high-quality, accessible, and lower-cost obstetric services in low-resource, marginalized communities.
mod_finding: The study validated quality outcomes for repeat cesarean sections performed by family physicians.
followup_time: From prenatal care through early childcare.
